title: JitAI Technical Whitepaper
intro: The AI-native paradigm: development and operations working as one
Embedded AI · Full system visibility · Development inside the application · A continuous development and runtime loop

title: Two barriers to enterprise AI adoption
intro: Employees already have AI assistants, but real business value remains inside systems that AI struggles to enter
notes: The core issue is where agents operate and whether they specialize, rather than model capability alone

cards.title: Barrier one: general-purpose agents remain outside the system
paragraphs: API access reveals only function names, parameters and return values
Business objects, field semantics, relationships and state rules remain invisible
Agents cannot execute accurately or reason from the complete business context

cards.title: Barrier two: general-purpose agents lack task specialization
paragraphs: One general-purpose agent handles every business task
It lacks focus, depth and domain-specific decision criteria
Capabilities stay on individual desktops, outside shared governance and reuse

title: What kind of system can overcome these barriers?
intro: To bring AI inside and align systems with the business, four requirements must be met together
notes: All four are essential: specialization provides expertise, embedding brings AI inside, and business twins with AI-friendly design provide visibility and understanding

cards.title: Specialized agents
paragraphs: Build dedicated agents for each business function
Each function focuses on its own responsibilities and decision criteria

cards.title: Embedded agents
paragraphs: Agents operate inside the system rather than as external tools
The runtime schedules them under shared governance

cards.title: Business twins
paragraphs: The system mirrors the real business
Business objects, processes and rules have corresponding system representations

cards.title: AI-friendly systems
paragraphs: AI can perceive and understand the system
AI can invoke and operate its capabilities

title: Development becomes the bottleneck: customization and fragmented AI context
notes: Conclusion: effective AI system development first requires continuity of information across the development process

cards.title: Traditional development: deep customization means high cost, long timelines and difficult maintenance
paragraphs: A system meeting all four requirements must be built around the enterprise's actual business and cannot be replaced by generic software
Traditional custom development requires substantial investment, slow delivery and costly changes

cards.title: Introducing AI development: AI coding delivers only about 15% overall efficiency improvement
paragraphs: Root cause: information is fragmented across requirements, design, coding, validation, release and operations
AI cannot see the whole system and its context, leaving an unbounded range of errors that is hard to resolve
Generated code receives no automatic feedback; errors are discovered through manual testing

title: The concept: two dimensions of AI-native design
intro: The chain of problems points to two dimensions that must both be AI-native
notes: These two dimensions form the element runtime and element development tracks that follow

cards.title: 1. AI-native application systems
paragraphs: The runtime dimension: help operational AI understand the system
Every system module is a standardized, self-describing element
AI can see and understand every module
Including models, services, workflows, permissions, states and their constraints

cards.title: 2. AI-native application development technology
paragraphs: The development dimension: help development AI understand what it is building
AI can see lifecycle information for the module being developed
Definitions, responsibilities, code, specifications, validation and runtime results
Requirements through operations are connected, allowing errors to converge

title: JitAI: one element runtime and specification for both AI-native dimensions
notes: Systems can closely match enterprise needs with much lower customization and maintenance costs. Development and operations share one foundation for both AI-native dimensions.

cards.title: 1. Design an abstract application system model
paragraphs: Define system layers, element types and responsibility boundaries
Use system-level knowledge to guide AI architectural decomposition

cards.title: 2. Express system modules as elements
paragraphs: Standardized and self-describing
Hot plugging and hot loading

cards.title: 3. Unify development and operations
paragraphs: One system model, specification, runtime, architecture and technology framework
Development can also drive the runtime

cards.title: 4. Connect both directions
paragraphs: Development can observe and drive operations
Operations can provide feedback to development

title: The essence of AI-native design: embedded AI with full system visibility
intro: Both development and runtime AI should see and understand the full system and every element from inside it

cards.title: Traditional approach: disconnected external tools
paragraphs: Development tools sit outside the system architecture
Runtime agents operate outside the business system
Development AI cannot see the full lifecycle of its development targets
Runtime AI can call APIs but cannot see the complete business context

cards.title: JitAI: embedded and connected
paragraphs: Development technology is part of the architecture itself
AI operates inside the system rather than as an external tool
Development AI can see the full system and all elements
Runtime AI can also see the whole system and interact through business objects for complete perception

extras.title: The structure of this whitepaper
paragraphs: Two parallel tracks: element development and element runtime. Each follows the same sequence: background problems → design principles → the JitAI approach
The tracks connect: development produces conforming elements → runtime loads and executes them → execution results return to development for iteration

title: Six structural gaps in traditional AI development
notes: Shared root cause: AI is external, without full system context, unified architectural constraints or a standardized output contract

cards.title: Semantic gap
paragraphs: AI does not actively clarify ambiguous requirements and implements the simplest interpretation
Root cause: no requirement clarification mechanism

cards.title: Context gap
paragraphs: Limited context windows cannot hold all materials, and content in the middle can be overlooked
Root cause: no structured context

cards.title: Lifecycle gap
paragraphs: AI is responsible only for writing code, excluding upstream requirements and downstream deployment and operations
Root cause: separation of development and operations

cards.title: Feedback gap
paragraphs: Generated code receives no automatic feedback; errors depend on manual testing
Root cause: no runtime-feedback loop

cards.title: Memory gap
paragraphs: Context and requirement clarification disappear between sessions, forcing repeated explanations
Root cause: no persistent design document

cards.title: Observability gap
paragraphs: AI cannot see where code runs, where it fails or who calls it
Root cause: no runtime observability

title: The JitAI approach: standardization and integration expose the system, element details and the full lifecycle to AI
intro: Three development principles address the causes of the six gaps
notes: Goal: move AI development from free-form coding to structured production governed by knowledge and contracts

cards.title: A correct system-wide design perspective
paragraphs: The abstract application model holds system knowledge and element responsibilities, enabling accurate architectural decomposition while maintaining a correct view of the whole system

cards.title: Precise element development specifications
paragraphs: Element specifications form the sole contract for development and operations. Standardizing smaller system modules constrains generation, improves accuracy and makes errors enumerable

cards.title: An embedded loop: development, operations and feedback
paragraphs: Development AI is embedded in the system and can see runtime results and exceptions, creating an automated development, validation and iteration loop

title: The abstract application model and element type system

cards.title: Abstract application model: system-level knowledge
paragraphs: Define common layers of enterprise application systems
Define responsibilities and collaboration between layers
Define element reference and invocation rules
Each node in the model represents an element type

cards.title: Element types: knowledge of type responsibilities
paragraphs: Every type has a clear position in the system
Specify field structures, public capabilities and modification boundaries
Specify validation methods and architectural ownership
Models · Services · Pages · Workflows · Events · Agents · Roles…

extras.title: How this guides development AI
paragraphs: When designing an application's element architecture, AI reads system-model knowledge and type responsibilities to produce accurate system decomposition and element designs from the outset

title: SDD specification-driven development and element source control

cards.title: Type specifications as upfront constraints
paragraphs: Specifications are enforced by Types and validation tools rather than AI discretion
When specifications do not cover a scenario, stop and report the gap instead of inventing behavior
When specifications conflict with implementation, use implementation source as the authority

cards.title: Elements are standardized source modules
paragraphs: Development AI generates source code and delivers it as elements
Conversational development means business users normally need not touch source code
Source remains visible and editable, allowing manual changes

comparisons.title: Traditional AI coding
paragraphs: Free-form coding with unbounded error types, guided by individual prompts

comparisons.title: Specification-driven generation (SDD)
paragraphs: People write specifications to generate source, followed by compilation and deployment

comparisons.title: JitAI
paragraphs: Type constraints generate standardized elements; development and runtime are unified without a separate compile-and-deploy step

title: Structured context and design-document management
notes: Persist facts—source, design documents, element inventories, tasks and logs—so work continues across sessions and assistants

cards.title: Context: from one-time injection to retrieval on demand
paragraphs: Traditional approach: a fixed, limited context window requires people to split tasks and choose materials
JitAI: addressable context retrieved on demand
One element is the smallest independently buildable and verifiable unit
Read only the current Type specification and direct dependencies
Content outside the target scope stays outside the context
Context becomes a retrieval problem rather than a capacity problem

cards.title: Design documents: mandatory clarification and persistence
paragraphs: Application design documents have states: draft → confirmed
Drafts record confirmed facts, public sources, inferences, assumptions and open questions; they are not implementation authority
Confirm scope, role permissions, state transitions, exceptions and acceptance criteria individually
Unresolved ambiguity prevents confirmation
Make ambiguity explicit · Carry clarification downstream · Separate facts from inferences

title: Six automated checks across the development lifecycle
intro: Completion means passing all six checks. Writing files, parsing JSON or building successfully is not sufficient
notes: Value: elements meet type contracts and load safely; production validation continually returns exceptions for improvement

cards.title: Validation is feedback
paragraphs: Development validation errors, runtime exceptions and logs return directly to development AI, creating an automated hypothesis → validation → modification → revalidation loop

cards.title: Repair threshold
paragraphs: Limit repairs on the same object to five attempts, then transfer to a person to prevent repeated iteration in the wrong direction

steps.title: 1 Source checks
paragraphs: Syntax, specifications and types

steps.title: 2 App relationships
paragraphs: Complete reference and dependency relationships

steps.title: 3 Build checks
paragraphs: Produce frontend and backend runtime resources

steps.title: 4 Loading checks
paragraphs: Address resolution and registration

steps.title: 5 Functional validation
paragraphs: Run with data in a pre-release environment

steps.title: 6 Runtime validation
paragraphs: Production execution with exception feedback

title: Four structural defects in current AI application patterns, such as desktop agents with ERP
notes: Shared root cause: AI is outside the system, and the system was not designed for AI

cards.title: 01 External AI
paragraphs: Agents run on employee desktops or in the cloud and use APIs. Outside the architecture, they cannot see the full system or element structure

cards.title: 02 Systems are not AI-native
paragraphs: Legacy systems center on tables and pages, without AI-readable object models, field semantics or constraints. Agents see interfaces but not business objects

cards.title: 03 Disconnected judgment and execution
paragraphs: Rules are duplicated in systems and agents and inevitably diverge. Chained API calls hide intermediate states and make failures difficult to roll back

cards.title: 04 Missing governance
paragraphs: Integration accounts have coarse API-level permissions, while desktop skills and prompts cannot be audited or upgraded centrally

title: The JitAI approach: an element architecture with embedded AI
intro: Three runtime principles address the four structural defects
notes: Goal: embedded runtime AI with full visibility, clear responsibilities and deterministic controls

cards.title: AI as a first-class element
paragraphs: Agents are dedicated elements sharing specifications, builds and governance with business elements, scheduled by the runtime

cards.title: Separate intelligence from functions
paragraphs: AI handles non-deterministic reasoning, including interpretation, judgment and decisions based on knowledge, experience and thinking frameworks;
Runtime services deterministically execute strongly consistent calculations, inventory updates and state transitions

cards.title: Unified governance
paragraphs: Elements and agents share RBAC, data scope and audit trails; permissions determine AI visibility

title: Five layers of a unified AI-native application architecture
intro: JitAI application architecture is the overarching concept, not a runtime entity. Its executable entities and contracts form the layers below
notes: Every layer follows the same Type specifications and namespaces. Upper-layer elements call only lower-layer public capabilities, never their source directly.
The runtime loads and schedules all elements by contract, giving development and runtime AI a complete system environment and full visibility.

layers.title: Element specifications: contract layer
paragraphs: Type definitions · Public capability contracts · Permission models · Namespaces shared by development and operations

layers.title: Entry layer
paragraphs: Messaging channels (Feishu / DingTalk / WeCom) · Business portals · External website embedding · Open APIs

layers.title: Agent element layer
paragraphs: Business agents · Long-running agents · Workflow orchestration agents · Skills · Plugins

layers.title: Business application elements
paragraphs: Models · Services · Pages and portals · Workflows · Events · Scheduled tasks

layers.title: Foundation elements
paragraphs: Element runtime · Databases · Cache · Object storage · Organizations and roles · Authorization · Auditing · Message queues

title: Two modes, one source: AI and people share the same business context
notes: AI and people use the same capabilities, without a second set of rules, permissions or entry points
Firm boundary: agents never write directly to the database. Changes use standardized business operations for financial consistency and auditability

cards.title: Business agents: runtime AI
paragraphs: Understand intent → Select authorized services → Record actions

cards.title: People: manual operations
paragraphs: Forms · Pages · Portals · Approvals

extras.title: Shared business foundation: a single source of truth
paragraphs: The same data models
The same service functions
The same authorization checks
The same audit trails

title: Deterministic execution: precise programmatic logic stays outside the model
notes: Models analyze and judge; they do not execute financial, inventory or state changes

cards.title: Language models: non-deterministic reasoning
paragraphs: Understand goals, analyze situations and explain changes
Identify exceptions, propose solutions and handle ambiguity

cards.title: System services: deterministic logic
paragraphs: Calculate amounts, deduct inventory and manage batch states
Check permissions, execute approval transactions and reconcile accounts

extras.title: Responsibilities in real business questions: models provide evidence and systems execute decisions

examples.title: Can this order ship?
paragraphs: AI summarizes customer credit and history
The system applies credit and release rules

examples.title: Can this batch be released?
paragraphs: AI retrieves inspection criteria and history
The system determines batch status and release

examples.title: Do these balances reconcile?
paragraphs: AI compares differences and explains exceptions
The system calculates amounts and reconciliation relationships

title: Agents as dedicated elements: modular and customized
notes: Agent capabilities are elements too: the same specifications, builds, acceptance checks and records as business functions, including controlled entry points, minimal page context, result writeback and runtime records

cards.title: Business agents
paragraphs: Operate real business objects and workflows

cards.title: Long-running agents
paragraphs: Asynchronous extended execution, including unattended operation

cards.title: Workflow orchestration
paragraphs: Coordinate multi-step processes across activities

cards.title: Embedded in external websites
paragraphs: Expose controlled business intelligence to external users

extras.title: One focused agent per business function, instead of one general-purpose agent
paragraphs: Sales, procurement, warehousing, production, quality, finance, HR and management operate within their own data, rules and permissions
Function-specific responsibilities · Focused expertise · Isolation to contain failures

title: Unified security and governance
notes: External access: API authentication · External client authorization · Third-party organization synchronization · Request-level cross-cutting processing

cards.title: Shared RBAC and data scope
paragraphs: Organizations, roles and data scope apply equally to people and agents
Agents can perform exactly the business capabilities they are authorized to use

cards.title: Authorization before invocation
paragraphs: Backend authorization, not interface visibility, controls access
Checks are specific to roles, workflow steps and data scope

cards.title: End-to-end runtime records and auditing
paragraphs: Backend requests, element execution, business exceptions and build diagnostics
Every business action is traceable and supports rollback

cards.title: Sensitive-data filtering
paragraphs: Keep secrets out of logs and raw variable values out of model context
Do not persist sensitive data; permissions determine what is visible

title: The two-track loop: development within the architecture, operations feeding development

cards.title: Element development
paragraphs: Read the abstract system model
Generate elements by Type specifications
Six automated checks
Deliver conforming element packages

cards.title: Element specifications: the shared contract
paragraphs: Type definitions · Public capabilities
Permission models · Namespaces

cards.title: Element runtime
paragraphs: Load elements by contract
Execute business logic and transitions
Runtime AI reasons and coordinates
Output states, exceptions and logs

extras.title: The value of the loop
paragraphs: Development output becomes executable runtime elements. States, exceptions and logs return internally to development AI as runtime validation, the sixth check, driving continuous correction and iteration.
Development technology belongs to the architecture and development AI operates inside the system, fundamentally different from external AI tools.

title: Deployment and integration options

cards.title: Deployment options
paragraphs: Private deployment: enterprise-owned infrastructure and data boundary
Multi-tenant SaaS: centrally hosted by the platform
Hybrid deployment: private core data with cloud-based peripheral capabilities

cards.title: Model gateway
paragraphs: Support multiple language-model providers through one interface
No dependency on a single model provider
Route by scenario: models handle judgment, services handle precise logic

extras.title: External systems and communication channels
paragraphs: Messaging channels: Feishu, DingTalk and WeCom allow employees to perform business operations in conversations
Third-party systems connect through standard services and events without duplicating business rules
Open APIs expose controlled capabilities with full authorization and auditing

title: Industry positioning: external AI tools are not AI-native architecture
notes: The core difference: other approaches lack a unified element type system derived from an abstract application model and a shared contract connecting development with operations. Their AI remains outside the architecture without full system visibility.

title: Platform boundaries and technical direction

cards.title: Responsibilities the platform does not assume
paragraphs: Replacing people in final business decisions
Performing exact financial and inventory calculations through AI; services handle these
General-purpose office and creative work
No dependency on a single model provider
Element modeling has a cost and requires acceptance testing with real data

cards.title: Technical direction
paragraphs: Continually improve element specifications
Industry templates and reusable element libraries
A marketplace for reusable skills and specialized agents
Partner-built Types and industry solutions

extras.title: Human-AI collaboration
paragraphs: People set goals, handle exceptions and retain final responsibility. AI executes, reasons and records its actions. Collaboration, not an unstaffed enterprise

title: Summary: AI-native development and architecture working as one
intro: AI-native means AI lives inside the system and can see the whole system and every element
Development technology belongs to the architecture; development AI and runtime AI are both first-class elements
The abstract application model provides knowledge and element specifications provide the shared contract
The two-track loop: development produces conforming elements, runtime executes them and returns feedback

extras.title: Q & A
paragraphs: Build AI-native enterprise systems with AI, and let AI drive business operations.
